# Dependencies & Preparation

First we import the required libraries and set up the paths.
We also assume that the `coderdata` package is installed and available in the Python environment. 

We can then download the latest version of the coderdata dataset, using the following command in the terminal:

```{bash}
#| label: download data
#| warning: FALSE
#| eval: FALSE
#| echo: FALSE
coderdata download --local_path '/tmp'
```

We can now set up `reticulate` to interface with Python from R.


```{r}
#| label: imports-and-setup
#| warning: FALSE
#| echo: FALSE

# r libraries
library(reticulate)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(patchwork)
library(dplyr)
library(GSVA) ##do to the enrichment statistics

# path setupd
data_dir <- "/tmp/"

#wd <- tempdir()
#setwd(wd)
reticulate::use_virtualenv('r-reticulate')
reticulate::import("coderdata")

# defines the python environment to use
py_require("coderdata")

# import the coderdata package from python
cd <- import("coderdata")


```


# Omics import
Now we are ready to load the datasets and format them for analysis. We will load the
 cell line datasets to load the relevant experimental,
drug, proteomic, and transcriptomic data for each dataset.

Note how this is done using the `reticulate` functionality to call Python functions from R via `cd$load(...)` and `datasets[[name]]$format(...)`.

```{r}
#| label: load-datasets
#| warning: false
#| echo: false


cell_lines <- c("ccle", "ctrpv2", "gcsi",
 "prism", "gdscv1", "gdscv2", "nci60",'fimm')

##actually only need to load 2 datasets
cell_lines <- c('gdscv2','ctrpv2')
exvivo <- c('beataml','bladder','pancreatic','sarcoma','colorectal','liver','mpnst','hcmi','cptac')

datasets <- list()

for (name in c(cell_lines, exvivo)) {
  datasets[[name]] <- cd$load(name, local_path = data_dir)
}

dataset_colors <- list(
  hcmi = '#EE7733',
  liver = '#004488',
  sarcoma  ='#882288',
  bladder = '#EE3377',
  cptac = '#CC3311',
  pancreatic = '#009988',
  colorectal = '#5544AA',
  beataml = '#6699CC',
  mpnst = '#BBBBBB',
  Sanger = '#999933',
  DepMap = '#DDCC77'
)
```


Now we have the transcripts data, each as a matrix. We can take a set of genes and identify 
specific drugs that are correlated with samples that are active in those.

## Panel A: Copy number

Let's plot copy number types across datasets. 

```{r}
#| label: plot-copynumber
#| warning: false

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

##collect copy number data from both datasets. treating
##cell lines differently because its only really 2 datasets
cl_cn <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cell_lines, function(ds){
  datasets[[ds]]$copy_number |> 
    left_join(datasets[[ds]]$genes) |>
    dplyr::rename(dataset = study)|>
    select(copy_call,dataset, improve_sample_id,gene_symbol)|>
    distinct()
})) #|>
  #distinct() #obviously this is kind of a pain and time consuming

ev_cn <- do.call(rbind, lapply(exvivo, function(ds){
  cv <- datasets[[ds]]$copy_number 
  if (!is.null(cv))
    return(cv|> mutate(dataset=ds)|>
     left_join(datasets[[ds]]$genes)  |>
     select(copy_call,dataset, improve_sample_id,gene_symbol)|>
    distinct())
}))

comb <- rbind(cl_cn, ev_cn)

##now how can we plot these?
##play around with counting and plotting
tot_counts <- comb |>
  group_by(dataset) |> summarize(total_genes = n_distinct(gene_symbol))

scounts <- comb|>group_by(dataset)|> summarize(samples = n_distinct(improve_sample_id))

print(tot_counts)

var_counts <- comb |> 
  group_by(copy_call, dataset, improve_sample_id) |> 
  summarize(`genes per sample` = n_distinct(gene_symbol)) |>
  left_join(scounts)

var_counts$`Copy Call` = factor(var_counts$copy_call,levels=c('deep del','het loss','diploid','gain','amp'))

count_sum <- var_counts |> 
  group_by(`Copy Call`,dataset,samples) |>
  summarize(`mean genes per sample` = mean(`genes per sample`))

##plot all the counts
##density seems to work? 
ggplot(var_counts, aes(x=`genes per sample`, y =`Copy Call`,fill=dataset))+# alpha = log(samples))) + 
  #geom_bar(stat='identity', position = 'dodge') + 
  geom_boxplot()+
  scale_fill_manual(values = dataset_colors)+
  scale_color_manual(values = dataset_colors)+
  theme_minimal(base_size=12)+
  scale_x_log10()
  #scale_fill_viridis_d()

ggsave('fig2a_cnv.pdf',width=8)
```


## Panel B: Mutations
Now we can do the same with mutation types.

```{r}
#| label: mutations


cl_mu <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cell_lines, function(ds){
  cv <- datasets[[ds]]$mutations|>
     left_join(datasets[[ds]]$genes)  |>
     select(variant_classification,dataset = study, improve_sample_id,gene_symbol) 
   distinct(cv)
  #cv[,c('entrez_id','variant_classification','improve_sample_id','study')] |> 
  #  dplyr::rename(dataset = study) 
}) )

ev_mu <- do.call(rbind, lapply(exvivo, function(ds){
  cv <- datasets[[ds]]$mutations 
  #print(paste(names(cv),collapse=','))
  if (!is.null(cv))
    return(cv|>
     left_join(datasets[[ds]]$genes)  |>
     select(variant_classification,improve_sample_id,gene_symbol) |>
     mutate(dataset=ds)|>
     distinct())
})) 

comb <- rbind(cl_mu, ev_mu)

comb |> group_by(variant_classification) |> 
  summarize(ndatasets=n_distinct(dataset)) 

comb |>  
  group_by(variant_classification, dataset, improve_sample_id) |> 
  summarize(`genes per sample` = n_distinct(gene_symbol)) |> 
 # group_by(variant_classification, dataset) |>
  #summarize(`Average genes per sample` = mean(genes_per_sample)) |>
  subset(!variant_classification %in% c('IGR','De_novo_Start_OutOfFrame','De_novo_Start_InFrame','Undetermined')) |>
  dplyr::rename(`Variant Classification`='variant_classification') |>
  ggplot(aes(x= `Variant Classification`, y= `genes per sample`, fill = dataset)) + 
  scale_y_log10()+
  geom_boxplot() +
#  geom_bar(stat='identity',position='dodge') +  
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values= dataset_colors) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

ggsave('fig2b_variants.pdf',width=8,height=8)

```

This is too many, and most aren't in all datasets

```{r}

common <-  comb |> group_by(variant_classification) |> 
  summarize(ndatasets=n_distinct(dataset)) |> subset(ndatasets>5)

comb |> subset(variant_classification %in% common$variant_classification)|>
  group_by(variant_classification, dataset, improve_sample_id) |> summarize(n_genes = n_distinct(gene_symbol)) |> ggplot(aes(x=n_genes, y=dataset, fill=variant_classification, alpha = 0.5)) + ggridges::geom_density_ridges2() +scale_x_log10() 
```

## Panel C: Transcriptomics

We combine the transriptomics and can do a quick sanity check to evaluate how they are 
distributed. Typically I do this across samples in a dataset, so this is a very
rough estimate.

```{r}
#| label: transcriptomics
#| warning: false

cl_tr <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cell_lines, function(ds){
  cv <- datasets[[ds]]$transcriptomics|>
     left_join(datasets[[ds]]$genes)  |>
     select(transcriptomics,dataset = study, improve_sample_id,gene_symbol) |>
     distinct() 
})) 

ev_tr <- do.call(rbind, lapply(exvivo, function(ds){
  #print(ds)
  cv <- datasets[[ds]]$transcriptomics 
  if (!is.null(cv))
    return(cv|>
     left_join(datasets[[ds]]$genes)  |>
     select(transcriptomics,improve_sample_id,gene_symbol) |>
     mutate(dataset=ds)|>
     distinct())
})) 

comb <- rbind(cl_tr, ev_tr)

comb$dataset[comb$dataset =='Sanger & Broad Cell Lines RNASeq']<-'Sanger'

ggplot(comb, aes(x=dataset, y = transcriptomics))+ 
  geom_boxplot() + scale_y_log10() 
```

Now for the real question: how do the different samples plot? I use UMAP instead of
PCA here because the clusters are more distinct. 

```{r}
#| label: rna-umap
#library(ggfortify)
library(umap) 

nu <- comb |>
  tidyr::unite(dataset, improve_sample_id, col='sample',sep='-', remove=FALSE) 


cmat <- nu[,c('gene_symbol','transcriptomics','sample')] |> 
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from='sample',
    values_from='transcriptomics',values_fn=mean)

cm <- tibble::column_to_rownames(cmat,'gene_symbol') |>
  drop_na()

pats <- nu[,c('sample','dataset')] |>
  distinct() #|>
  #subset(dataset!='beataml')

cols <- intersect(colnames(cm),pats$sample)
#pca <- prcomp(t(cm[,cols]))
#autoplot(pca, data=subset(pats, sample%in%cols),color='dataset')

cmm <- log2(cm + 1)
tumap = umap(t(cmm[,cols]), n_components = 2, random_state = 15) 

layout <- tumap[["layout"]] 
layout <- data.frame(layout) 
final <- cbind(layout, subset(pats, sample%in%cols)) 



ggplot(final, aes(x=X1,y=X2,col=dataset,alpha=0.8)) +geom_point() + 
  ggtitle("UMAP of log TPM of RNA-Seq datasets")+
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)+
  scale_color_manual(values = dataset_colors)

ggsave('fig2c_transcripts.pdf',width=8)

```

Should we try a PCA now that we have more data?

```{r}
library(ggfortify)

pcr <- prcomp(t(cmm[,cols]))

autoplot(pcr, data=subset(pats, sample%in%cols), color='dataset',alpha=0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values= dataset_colors)

ggsave('fig2c_transcripts_pca.pdf',width=8)
```

## Panel D: Proteomics

Lastly we can look at the proteomics values and see how they are distributed. 

```{r}
#| label: proteomics


cl_pr <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cell_lines, function(ds){
  cv <- datasets[[ds]]$proteomics|>
     left_join(datasets[[ds]]$genes)  |>
     select(proteomics,dataset = study, improve_sample_id,gene_symbol) |>
     distinct()  
}))  #obviously this is kind of a pain and time consuming

ev_pr <- do.call(rbind, lapply(exvivo, function(ds){
  #print(ds)
  cv <- datasets[[ds]]$proteomics 
  if (!is.null(cv)){
    ##lets try some corrections
   # if(ds=='liver')
   #   cv$proteomics = log2(2**cv$proteomics-1)
   # else if(ds=='beataml')
   #   cv$proteomics = 2**cv$proteomics
    #else if(ds=='cptac')
    #  cv$proteomics = 2**cv$proteomics
    return(cv|>
     left_join(datasets[[ds]]$genes)  |>
     select(proteomics,dataset = study, improve_sample_id,gene_symbol) |>
     distinct()|>
    mutate(dataset=ds))
  }
}))

comb <- rbind(cl_pr, ev_pr)

#ggplot(comb, aes(x=dataset, y = proteomics))+ 
#  geom_boxplot() + scale_y_log10() 

```

We can also experiment with a UMAP for these datasets.

```{r}
#| label: proteomics umap


nu <- comb |>
  tidyr::unite(dataset, improve_sample_id, col='sample',sep='-', remove=FALSE) 


cmat <- nu[,c('gene_symbol','proteomics','sample')] |> 
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from='sample',
    values_from='proteomics',values_fn=function(x) mean(x,na.rm=T))#values_fill=0.0)

cm <- tibble::column_to_rownames(cmat,'gene_symbol') |>
  drop_na()

pats <- nu[,c('sample','dataset')] |>
  distinct() #|>
  #subset(dataset!='beataml')

cols <- intersect(colnames(cm),pats$sample)
#pca <- prcomp(t(cm[,cols]))
#autoplot(pca, data=subset(pats, sample%in%cols),color='dataset')

cmm <- cm#a1pply(cm,2,function(x) (x-mean(x))/sd(x))#cm#log2(cm + 1)
tumap = umap(t(cmm[,cols]), n_components = 2, random_state = 15) 

layout <- tumap[["layout"]] 
layout <- data.frame(layout) 
final <- cbind(layout, subset(pats, sample%in%cols)) 

ggplot(final, aes(x=X1,y=X2,col=dataset,alpha=0.8)) +geom_point() + 
  ggtitle("UMAP of Z-scored Proteomics datasets")+
  scale_color_manual(values = dataset_colors) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

ggsave('fig2d_proteomics.pdf',width=8)

```

Now that we have the four figures we can assemble into a single omics QC plo


```{r}
#| label: proteomics pca
#| 

library(ggfortify)

pcr <- prcomp(t(cm[,cols]))

autoplot(pcr, data=subset(pats, sample%in%cols), color='dataset',alpha=0.8) +
  ggtitle("PCA of un-centered proteomics")+
  scale_color_manual(values = dataset_colors) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

ggsave('fig2c_proteomics_pca.pdf',width=8)

```
